# Electric

> Electric provides the data primitives and infra to build collaborative, multi-agent systems. Including Postgres Sync, Durable Streams, TanStack DB and PGlite.

> [!IMPORTANT] Instructions for coding agents
> Coding agents should read [AGENTS.md](https://electric.ax/AGENTS.md) for instructions and guidance.

## Table of Contents

### Hosted products

- [Electric Streams](https://electric.ax/streams.md): The data primitive for the agent loop. Persistent, addressable, real-time streams over plain HTTP.
- [Electric Sync](https://electric.ax/sync.md): Composable sync primitives for multi-agent systems — Postgres Sync, TanStack DB and PGlite.

### Sync primitives

- [Postgres Sync](https://electric.ax/sync/postgres-sync.md): Read-path sync engine for Postgres that handles partial replication, data delivery and fan-out.
- [TanStack DB](https://electric.ax/sync/tanstack-db.md): Reactive client store for building super-fast apps. With sub-millisecond reactivity and instant local writes.
- [PGlite](https://electric.ax/sync/pglite.md): Embeddable Postgres with reactivity and sync. For a full database inside your client or runtime.

### Guides

- [Auth - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/auth.md): How to do authentication and authorization with Electric.
- [Shapes - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/shapes.md): Shapes are the core primitive for controlling sync in the ElectricSQL system.
- [Writes - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/writes.md): How to do local writes and write-path sync with Electric.
- [Installation - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/installation.md): How to install and run Electric.
- [PostgreSQL Permissions - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/postgres-permissions.md): How to create and configure PostgreSQL users with the necessary permissions for Electric.
- [Deployment - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/deployment.md): How to deploy the Electric sync engine.
- [Upgrading - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/upgrading.md): How to upgrade the Electric sync service with minimal disruption.
- [Sharding - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/sharding.md): How to use Electric with sharded PostgreSQL databases.
- [Security - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/security.md): How to secure data access and encrypt data with Electric.
- [Troubleshooting - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/troubleshooting.md): Tips and FAQs on how to run Electric successfully.
- [Client development - Guide](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/guides/client-development.md): How to write an Electric client for any language that speaks HTTP and JSON.

### API

- [HTTP API](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/api/http.md): The HTTP API is the primary, low level API for syncing data with Electric.
- [Sync service](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/api/config.md): Configuration options for the Electric sync engine.

#### Clients

- [Typescript Client](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/api/clients/typescript.md): Electric provides an Typescript client for streaming Shapes from Postgres into the web browser and other Javascript environments.
- [Elixir Client](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/api/clients/elixir.md): Electric provides an Elixir client and a Phoenix integration.

### Integrations

#### Frameworks

- [LiveStore - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/livestore.md): How to use Electric with LiveStore.
- [MobX - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/mobx.md): How to use Electric with MobX.
- [Next.js - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/next.md): How to use Electric with Next.js.
- [Phoenix - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/phoenix.md): How to use Electric with Phoenix.
- [React - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/react.md): How to use Electric with React.
- [Redis - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/redis.md): How to use Electric to sync data into Redis.
- [TanStack - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/tanstack.md): How to use Electric with TanStack. Including using Electric for read-path sync and TanStack Query for optimistic writes.
- [Yjs - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/yjs.md): How to use Electric with Yjs.

#### Platforms

- [Amazon Web Services (AWS) - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/aws.md): How to deploy Electric on Amazon Web Services (AWS).
- [Cloudflare - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/cloudflare.md): How to use Electric with Cloudflare.
- [Crunchy Data - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/crunchy.md): How to use Electric with Crunchy Bridge managed Postgres.
- [Digital Ocean - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/digital-ocean.md): How to deploy Electric on Digital Ocean.
- [Expo - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/expo.md): How to use Electric to sync data into Expo apps.
- [Fly.io - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/fly.md): How to deploy Electric on Fly.
- [Google Cloud Platform (GCP) - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/gcp.md): How to deploy Electric on Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
- [Neon - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/neon.md): How to use Electric with Neon's serverless Postgres.
- [Netlify - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/netlify.md): How to deploy Electric apps on Netlify.
- [PlanetScale - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/planetscale.md): How to use Electric with PlanetScale Postgres.
- [Render - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/render.md): How to deploy Electric on Render.
- [Supabase - Integrations](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/integrations/supabase.md): How to use Electric with Supabase. Including syncing data out of Supabase Postgres and into Supabase Edge Functions.

### Reference

- [Alternatives](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/reference/alternatives.md): Alternative projects and systems for syncing data and building local-first applications.
- [Benchmarks - Reference](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/reference/benchmarks.md): We run benchmarks for the Electric sync engine and the Electric Cloud, which hosts the sync engine behind a CDN.
- [Literature](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/reference/literature.md): A selection of research papers that relate to local-first software and distributed databases.
- [Telemetry](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/reference/telemetry.md): Electric provides telemetry data for real-time system monitoring.

### Demo apps

- [Burn](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/burn.md): Agentic system built on Postgres and a real-time sync stack.
- [AI Chat](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/ai-chat.md): Resilient, multi-user, multi-agent AI chat app powered by Electric.
- [Linearlite](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/linearlite.md): Local-first project management app built with Electric and PGlite.
- [Notes](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/notes.md): Collaborative note-taking app with sync powered by Electric and Yjs.
- [Pixel art](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/pixel-art.md): Collaborative pixel art editor with real-time multiplayer editing.

### Technical examples

- [Bash](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/bash.md): Example using Electric from a bash script.
- [Encryption](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/encryption.md): Example of how to implement encryption with Electric.
- [Gatekeeper auth](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/gatekeeper-auth.md): Example of the gatekeeper pattern for API-based auth with Electric.
- [Next.js](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/nextjs.md): Example of an Electric app using Next.js.
- [Phoenix LiveView](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/phoenix-liveview.md): Example of a Phoenix LiveView app using Electric.
- [Proxy auth](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/proxy-auth.md): Example showing how to authorize access to Electric using a proxy.
- [React](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/react.md): Basic example of an Electric app using React.
- [Redis](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/redis.md): Example showing how to sync into Redis from Electric.
- [Remix](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/remix.md): Example of an Electric app using Remix.
- [Tanstack](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/tanstack.md): Example of an Electric app using Tanstack Query for optimistic state.
- [Todo app](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/todo-app.md): This is a classic TodoMVC example app, developed using Electric.
- [Write patterns](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/write-patterns.md): Four different patterns for handling writes in an Electric application.
- [Yjs](https://electric.ax/sync/demos/yjs.md): This is an example application using Electric with Yjs.

### Electric Sync

- [Electric Sync](https://electric.ax/sync.md): Composable sync primitives for multi-agent systems — Postgres Sync, TanStack DB and PGlite.

### Sync primitives

- [Postgres Sync](https://electric.ax/sync/postgres-sync.md): Read-path sync engine for Postgres that handles partial replication, data delivery and fan-out.
- [TanStack DB](https://electric.ax/sync/tanstack-db.md): Reactive client store for building super-fast apps. With sub-millisecond reactivity and instant local writes.
- [PGlite](https://electric.ax/sync/pglite.md): Embeddable Postgres with reactivity and sync. For a full database inside your client or runtime.

### Demo apps

- [Chat Starter](https://electric.ax/agents/demos/chat-starter.md): Multi-agent chatroom where philosopher agents debate, answer questions, and react to messages in real time.
- [Deep Survey](https://electric.ax/agents/demos/deep-survey.md): Multi-agent research app where an orchestrator coordinates a swarm of explorer agents to build a live knowledge base.

### Technical examples

- [Playground](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/examples/playground.md): Technical examples for experimenting with Electric Agents coordination patterns.

### Demo apps

- [Durable Doom](https://electric.ax/streams/demos/durable-doom.md): Doom on Durable Streams. Live spectating, time-travel, and fork-to-continue — all client-side, no backend.
- [Collaborative AI Editor](https://electric.ax/streams/demos/collaborative-ai-editor.md): Collaborative rich text editor where an AI agent is a server-side CRDT peer.
- [Territory Wars](https://electric.ax/streams/demos/territory-wars.md): Multiplayer territory capture game built with Yjs CRDTs on Durable Streams.

- [Benchmarks - Reference](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/reference/benchmarks.md): We run benchmarks for the Electric sync engine and the Electric Cloud, which hosts the sync engine behind a CDN.
- [Literature](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/reference/literature.md): A selection of research papers that relate to local-first software and distributed databases.
- [Telemetry](https://electric.ax/docs/sync/reference/telemetry.md): Electric provides telemetry data for real-time system monitoring.

- [Chat Starter](https://electric.ax/agents/demos/chat-starter.md): Multi-agent chatroom where philosopher agents debate, answer questions, and react to messages in real time.
- [Deep Survey](https://electric.ax/agents/demos/deep-survey.md): Multi-agent research app where an orchestrator coordinates a swarm of explorer agents to build a live knowledge base.

### Usage

- [Overview](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/overview.md): High level overview of the Electric Agents system and developer APIs.
- [Defining entities](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/defining-entities.md): Register entity types with the EntityRegistry, define custom state collections, typed schemas, and handler functions.
- [Writing handlers](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/writing-handlers.md): Implement entity handlers using HandlerContext and WakeEvent, with patterns for first wake, messaging, and tool use.
- [Configuring the agent](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/configuring-the-agent.md): Set up LLM agents with ctx.useAgent(), including model selection, system prompts, tools, and test responses.
- [Context composition](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/context-composition.md): Control what goes into the agent's context window using ctx.useContext() with token-budgeted sources, cache tiers, and imperative context entries.
- [Defining tools](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/defining-tools.md): Create stateless, stateful, and handler-scoped tools for the LLM agent loop.
- [Managing state](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/managing-state.md): Declare and manage persistent entity state using custom collections with typed CRUD operations.
- [Permissions & principals](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/permissions-and-principals.md): Control who can spawn, read, write, signal, fork, schedule, and manage Electric Agents entities using principals and grants.
- [Spawning & coordinating](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/spawning-and-coordinating.md): Spawn child entities, observe existing ones, send messages, and use EntityHandle for coordination.
- [Waking entities](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/waking-entities.md): How entity handlers get invoked - the triggers that produce wakes, how wake config threads through spawn/observe/observe(db(...)), and how to read a WakeEvent in a handler.
- [Signals](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/signals.md): Interrupt, pause, resume, terminate, and notify Electric Agents entities with lifecycle signals.
- [Sandboxing](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/sandboxing.md): Isolate file, process, and network access for LLM-driven tools with Electric Agents sandbox profiles.
- [Attachments](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/attachments.md): Upload, reference, read, and hydrate files and images for Electric Agents entities.
- [Shared state](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/shared-state.md): Coordinate across entities with shared state streams, schema definition, and cross-entity reads and writes.
- [Clients & React](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/clients-and-react.md): Observe Electric Agents entities from app code, build reactive StreamDB handles, and render chat timelines with the React useChat hook.
- [Programmatic runtime client](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/programmatic-runtime-client.md): Use createRuntimeServerClient to spawn entities, send messages, register wakes, manage schedules, and connect shared state from application code.
- [App setup](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/app-setup.md): Connect your app to the Electric Agents runtime with createRuntimeHandler, webhooks, and type registration.
- [Embedded built-ins](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/embedded-builtins.md): Embed the built-in Horton and worker runtime in your own process using @electric-ax/agents, BuiltinAgentsServer, or the entrypoint helpers.
- [Webhook sources](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/webhook-sources.md): Let agents discover and subscribe to external webhook-backed feeds that wake entities with matching event data.
- [MCP servers](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/mcp-servers.md): Connect agents to external tools, resources, and prompts via the Model Context Protocol. Register servers programmatically through the Registry API, declaratively in mcp.json, or globally in the desktop app's settings.
- [Testing](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/usage/testing.md): Test entity handlers with testResponses for LLM mocking, plus unit and integration testing patterns.

### Reference

- [CLI](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/cli.md): Command reference for the Electric Agents CLI: spawn, send, observe, inspect, list, and manage entities.
- [HandlerContext](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/handler-context.md): API reference for HandlerContext: state, coordination, agent configuration, and execution control.
- [EntityDefinition](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/entity-definition.md): Type reference for EntityDefinition: description, state, schemas, and handler function signature.
- [AgentConfig](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/agent-config.md): API reference for AgentConfig: system prompt, model, tools, streaming, and test responses.
- [AgentTool](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/agent-tool.md): Interface reference for AgentTool: name, description, TypeBox parameters schema, and execute function.
- [StateCollectionProxy](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/state-collection-proxy.md): API reference for StateCollectionProxy: insert, update, delete, get, and toArray operations.
- [EntityHandle](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/entity-handle.md): API reference for EntityHandle returned by spawn and observe: streams, status, and messaging.
- [SharedStateHandle](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/shared-state-handle.md): Type reference for SharedStateHandle: collection proxies and SharedStateSchemaMap interface.
- [WakeEvent](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/wake-event.md): Type reference for WakeEvent and Wake configuration: runFinished and change-based wake conditions.
- [Built-in collections](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/built-in-collections.md): Reference for the 20 runtime-managed collections: runs, steps, texts, toolCalls, inbox, signals, errors, slashCommands, and more.
- [EntityRegistry](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/entity-registry.md): API reference for EntityRegistry: define, get, list, and clear entity type registrations.
- [RuntimeHandler](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/runtime-handler.md): API reference for RuntimeHandler: webhook handling, type registration, and deployment configuration.
- [McpRegistry](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/mcp-registry.md): API reference for the MCP Registry — addServer, applyConfig, subscribe, reauthorize, and the lifecycle of an MCP server entry inside the runtime.
- [McpServerConfig](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/reference/mcp-server-config.md): Schema reference for MCP server entries — transports, auth modes, and persistence callbacks accepted by Registry.addServer, applyConfig, and the mcp.json / settings.json layers.

### Entities

#### Agents

- [Horton agent](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/entities/agents/horton.md): The built-in Horton assistant - chat, research, code, and dispatch subagents in one entity type.
- [Worker](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/entities/agents/worker.md): Generic sandboxed subagent type. Spawned by Horton (or any agent) via the spawn_worker tool with a system prompt and a chosen tool subset.

#### Patterns

- [Manager-Worker](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/entities/patterns/manager-worker.md): Coordination pattern where a parent spawns specialist children, waits for completion, and synthesizes results.
- [Pipeline](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/entities/patterns/pipeline.md): Sequential processing pattern where each stage's output feeds into the next via state transitions.
- [Map-Reduce](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/entities/patterns/map-reduce.md): Parallel processing pattern that splits work into chunks, processes simultaneously, and reduces results.
- [Dispatcher](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/entities/patterns/dispatcher.md): Message routing pattern that classifies incoming messages and dispatches to specialist agents.
- [Blackboard (shared state)](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/entities/patterns/blackboard.md): Multi-agent coordination using shared state as a common data structure for reads and writes.
- [Reactive observers](https://electric.ax/docs/agents/entities/patterns/reactive-observers.md): Pattern for entities that watch others and react to changes using ctx.observe() with wake conditions.

### Usage

- [CLI](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/cli.md): Command-line tool for creating, writing to, reading from, and managing Durable Streams. Supports piped input, JSON mode, batch writes, and token authentication.
- [JSON mode](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/json-mode.md): Stream structured data using JSON messages over a Durable Stream.
- [Durable Proxy](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/durable-proxy.md): Put durable, resumable streaming in front of existing AI streaming APIs. Persists upstream responses into Durable Streams so clients can reconnect and resume reads.
- [Durable State](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/durable-state.md): Structured state changes on top of Durable Streams. Work with typed insert, update, and delete events using MaterializedState, StreamDB, and Durable Sessions.
- [StreamDB](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/stream-db.md): Type-safe reactive database in a durable stream. Define schemas with StandardSchema, query with TanStack DB, and use optimistic actions on top of Durable State.
- [StreamFS](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/stream-fs.md): Shared filesystem for AI agents built on Durable Streams. Provides files, directories, metadata, content streams, and watch-based synchronization across agents.

#### Clients

- [TypeScript client](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/clients/typescript.md): TypeScript client for Durable Streams. Fetch-like stream() for reads and IdempotentProducer for exactly-once writes with batching and retries.
- [Python client](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/clients/python.md): Python client for Durable Streams with sync and async APIs. Generator-based stream consumption and IdempotentProducer for exactly-once writes.
- [Clients](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/clients/other.md): Durable Streams client libraries for a wide range of languages, including TypeScript, Python, Go, Elixir, .NET, Swift, PHP, Java, Rust, and Ruby.

### Integrations

- [TanStack AI](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/integrations/tanstack-ai.md): TanStack AI connection adapter for Durable Streams. Make chat sessions resumable, resilient, and shareable across tabs, devices, users and agents.
- [Vercel AI SDK](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/integrations/vercel-ai-sdk.md): Vercel AI SDK Transport that makes chat sessions resumable, resilient, and shareable across tabs, devices, users and agents.
- [Yjs](https://electric.ax/docs/streams/integrations/yjs.md): Sync Yjs CRDT documents over HTTP with automatic server-side compaction, snapshot management, and optional awareness (presence) support.
